shortDescription: The German year-ahead power contract reached another multi-year high on Monday, with prices at levels not seen since October 2023, as new strikes in the Middle East compounded supply concerns and drove up fuel prices.($1 = 0.8653 euros)

children: The German year-ahead power contract reached another multi-year high on Monday, with prices at levels not seen since October 2023, as new strikes in the Middle East compounded supply concerns and drove up fuel prices.
The German year-ahead contract (TRDEBYc1) was up 2.4% to €136 ($157) per megawatt hour at 0731 GMT, according to LSEG data.
"Latest developments with influence on the energy complex get the market to surge to new highs for nearby contracts this morning," analysts at Mind Energy wrote.
The equivalent French contract (TRDEBYc1) was untraded.
French nuclear availability rose by 3 percentage points to 73% of total capacity.

Strike notices have been filed at state-owned nuclear operator EDF, as energy sector unions plan to strike over a July recommendation by France's Court of Auditors to limit wage growth and curb employee benefits.
On the spot side, the German day-ahead contract (TRDEBD1) was down 31% to €177.50/MWh, as renewable power generation is set to pick up.
Consumption in Germany is expected to edge up by 0.8 gigawatts, while wind power output is set to more than double to 11.2 GW and solar power supply is expected to rise by 3.3 GW to 15.2 GW.
The equivalent French contract was not traded, according to LSEG data.
Consumption in France was set to rise by 2.1 GW, with wind power generation set to grow by 2.3 GW and solar power expected to be roughly stable at just shy of 6 GW.
The European carbon market's benchmark contract
was up 1.2% at €86.55 a metric ton.

title: German year-ahead power contract hits 2023 highs as fuel prices climb
